extraction_text: Bhima encounters Hanuman blocking his path in the forest.

relationships: Bhima is the son of Vayu (Wind God)
Hanuman is the son of Vayu (Wind God)
supernatural_elements: Hanuman is disguised as a monkey

extraction_text: Bhima introduces himself as the son of Kunti and Vayu, a Kuru descendant of the lunar dynasty.
Hanuman refuses to move, claiming illness, and challenges Bhima to step over him.

relationships: Hanuman tests Bhima's strength and character

extraction_text: Bhima refuses to step over Hanuman out of respect for the Supreme Soul within all beings.

relationships: Shows Bhima's adherence to dharma despite his strength

extraction_text: Bhima mentions Hanuman from the Ramayana as his brother who leaped across the ocean.

relationships: Bhima claims Hanuman as his brother (both sons of Vayu)
Hanuman is a heroic monkey king from the Ramayana

extraction_text: Bhima boasts of his strength equal to Hanuman's and threatens to kill the monkey if he doesn't move.

relationships: Bhima asserts his power over the disguised Hanuman

extraction_text: Hanuman, amused, asks Bhima to move his tail aside to pass.
Bhima tries but fails to move Hanuman's tail, despite using all his strength.
Bhima, ashamed, apologizes and asks Hanuman to reveal his true identity.

relationships: Hanuman's identity is about to be revealed

extraction_text: Hanuman acknowledges Bhima's curiosity and prepares to tell his story.

relationships: Hanuman will reveal his identity and connection to Bhima

extraction_text: Hanuman introduces himself to Bhima as the son of the Wind God (Vayu), born to Anjana, and a monkey named Hanuman.

attributes.relationships: Hanuman is the son of Vayu (Wind God) and Anjana; Bhima is a listener

extraction_text: Hanuman describes the monkey kings Sugriva and Vali, who are sons of Surya (Sun God) and Indra respectively, and mentions his friendship with Sugriva.

attributes.relationships: Sugriva and Vali are monkey kings; Hanuman is friends with Sugriva

extraction_text: Sugriva, due to some reason, was oppressed by his brother Vali and lived on Mount Rishyamukha with Hanuman for a long time.

attributes.relationships: Vali oppresses Sugriva; Hanuman accompanies Sugriva in exile

extraction_text: Vishnu incarnates as Rama, the mighty son of Dasharatha, and enters the Dandaka forest with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana to please his father.

attributes.relationships: Rama is an avatar of Vishnu, son of Dasharatha, husband of Sita, brother of Lakshmana

extraction_text: Ravana transforms into a deer, deceives Rama, and abducts Sita from Janasthana.

attributes.relationships: Ravana is the antagonist who abducts Sita, Rama's wife

extraction_text: Rama and Lakshmana search for Sita and meet Sugriva on a mountain peak, leading to a friendship between Rama and Sugriva.
Rama kills Vali and installs Sugriva as king, after which Sugriva sends monkeys to search for Sita.

attributes.relationships: Rama kills Vali; Sugriva becomes king and aids Rama

extraction_text: Hanuman leaps across a hundred-yojana-wide ocean to Lanka, finds Sita in Ravana's palace, gives her Rama's message, and returns.

attributes.relationships: Hanuman acts as Rama's emissary to Sita

extraction_text: Rama kills all the Rakshasas (demons), rescues Sita, and returns with her.

attributes.relationships: Rama defeats the Rakshasas and reunites with Sita

extraction_text: Before Rama's departure, Hanuman requests and is granted the boon of immortality as long as Rama's story is told in the world.

attributes.relationships: Rama grants Hanuman immortality linked to his own legend

extraction_text: Rama rules for eleven thousand years and then ascends to heaven.
Hanuman explains to Bhima that the path they are on is for gods only, not mortals, and that the lake Bhima seeks is nearby, warning him to avoid attacks or curses.

attributes.relationships: Hanuman protects Bhima as a fellow son of Vayu

extraction_text: Bhima, filled with joy upon hearing Hanuman's words, respectfully bows to his elder (Yudhishthira) and requests Hanuman to show his gigantic form from when he leaped across the ocean.

attributes.relationships: Bhima shows respect to Yudhishthira (his elder brother) and makes a request to Hanuman

extraction_text: Hanuman explains that his past form cannot be seen now because it belongs to a different time and era, and all beings must adapt to their current era.
Bhima asks Hanuman to explain the characteristics of different eras (Yugas), including behavior, dharma, and physical conditions.
Hanuman describes Satya Yuga (Krita Yuga) as the perfect age where dharma remains intact, there is no disease or conflict, and all beings fulfill their duties harmoniously.
Hanuman explains Treta Yuga where dharma decreases by one quarter, Vishnu becomes red, and people perform sacrifices and follow dharma diligently.
Hanuman describes Dvapara Yuga where dharma is reduced by half, Vishnu becomes yellow, and the Vedas are divided into four parts.
The text describes the decline of knowledge and righteousness across the Yugas (ages), starting with the Krita Yuga.

attributes.action: Degeneration of Vedic knowledge, truth, and dharma (righteousness)

extraction_text: In the Treta Yuga, knowledge of the Vedas becomes fragmented, truth is lost, and people become afflicted by diseases, desires, and calamities.

attributes.action: Further decline; people perform austerities and sacrifices with desire for heavenly rewards

extraction_text: In the Dvapara Yuga, due to the lack of dharma, beings are destroyed. By the Kali Yuga (the Dark Age of Strife), dharma is reduced to one quarter.

attributes.action: Destruction and severe reduction of righteousness

extraction_text: In the Kali Yuga, Vishnu becomes black (Krishna), Vedic customs, dharma, sacrifices, and rituals wane. Disasters, diseases, and suffering become prevalent.

attributes.action: Divine transformation and the exhaustion of sacred order

extraction_text: As the age declines, dharma declines; as dharma declines, the world declines; as the world declines, the forces that sustain it decline. In the declining age, dharma produces results contrary to desire.
The speaker states that the Kali Yuga will soon appear and long-lived beings will have to adapt to it.

The speaker (Markandeya) addresses the listener (Yudhishthira, referred to as 'Son of Kunti' and 'Tamer of Foes'), chiding his curiosity about these matters and the speaker's own identity as meaningless. He concludes the discourse on the ages and bids farewell.

attributes.action: Speaker rebuffs listener's curiosity and ends the narration
attributes.relationships: Markandeya (the sage) is narrating to Yudhishthira (the Pandava prince)
